title: SCAN: Neural Additive Networks for Scalable High-Order Component Selection and Estimation
abstract: arXiv:2611.30452v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Functional ANOVA models express a prediction as a sum of main effects and interactions, but existing neural functional ANOVA models require the interactions to be specified in advance, which forces a trade-off between missing higher-order structure and the cost of enumerating many interactions. We propose SCAN (Scalable Component Additive Networks), which learns which features each basis function combines, so that components of different orders are selected and estimated jointly without enumerating candidates. The learned component index sets form a small candidate collection on which post-hoc identification is carried out efficiently. A global component-selection parameter shares information across basis functions, and truncating negligible component-selection weights gives a sparse model that is identified after training. We establish universal approximation, a minimax optimal rate up to a logarithmic factor, and component selection

translated_title: SCAN：用于可扩展高阶成分选择与估计的神经加性网络
translated_abstract: 函数方差分析（ANOVA）模型将预测表示为主效应与交互效应之和，但现有的神经函数ANOVA模型需要预先指定交互项，这迫使研究者在遗漏高阶结构与枚举大量交互项的成本之间进行权衡。我们提出了SCAN（Scalable Component Additive Networks，可扩展成分加性网络），它学习每个基函数组合哪些特征，从而无需枚举候选即可联合地选择和估计不同阶数的成分。学习到的成分索引集形成一个小型候选集合，可在其上高效地进行事后识别。一个全局成分选择参数在基函数之间共享信息，截断可忽略的成分选择权重即可得到训练后可识别的稀疏模型。我们建立了万能逼近性、（在相差一个对数因子的意义下的）极小极大最优速率以及成分选择……
tldr: SCAN通过让每个基函数自动学习组合哪些特征，无需预先枚举交互项即可联合选择与估计不同阶数的成分，并具备万能逼近和极小极大最优速率等理论保证。
en_tdlr: SCAN learns which features each basis function combines, enabling joint selection and estimation of different-order components without enumerating interactions in advance, with theoretical guarantees of universal approximation and minimax optimal rates.
